official.deadline_note: No single applicant deadline is published. The official calendar sets dates for institutions: Call Notice release 29 June 2026, HEI/ICT proposals to CNPq until 13 August 2026, preliminary list of selected HEIs/ICTs November 2026, final list December 2026. From December 2026 each selected HEI/ICT runs its own candidate selection, so applicants must meet the deadline of the individual institution/Graduate Program (PPG) they apply to, with scholarships implemented between March 2027 and March 2028. The page warns that dates may change.
official.application_cycle: PEC-PG 2027 cycle - Chamada Publica CNPq/CAPES/MRE No. 16/2026, published 29 June 2026; eligible HEI/ICT list published December 2026; scholarships implemented March 2027 to March 2028
official.status_note: The 2027 Call Notice was released on 29 June 2026 and submissions from Brazilian institutions ran until 13 August 2026. CNPq will publish the final list of eligible HEIs/ICTs in December 2026, after which each institution selects candidates and implements scholarships from March 2027 to March 2028. The official page notes calendar dates may change.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The MRE About-the-program page states the PEC-PG student has the right to a 'free place in a Brazilian Higher Education Institution, for a postgraduate course' and a 'monthly scholarship in the same amount as that offered to Brazilian students'. No separate tuition-fee waiver wording is published.
benefits: Monthly stipend - R$ 2,100.00 for Master's degree (duration of 24 months) and R$ 3,100.00 for Doctorate degree (duration of 48 months).
Free place in a Brazilian Higher Education Institution, for a postgraduate course (monthly scholarship in the same amount as that offered to Brazilian students).
Access to the Brazilian Public Health System (SUS) - access throughout Brazil, on the same conditions as Brazilian citizens, without discrimination based on nationality or immigration status.

Financial aid to return to the country of origin - paid by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MRE), depending on budgetary and financial availability. The aid amount varies according to the country of origin and is defined in a table attached to MRE Ordinance No. 572/2024.
eligibility: Be a national of one of the countries participating in the Program and live in one of them (countries with an educational, cultural, or scientific and technological cooperation agreement in force with Brazil)
Not have Brazilian nationality (not having dual Brazilian nationality nor the right to it) and not have a permanent residence permit for Brazil
Have completed a higher education course equivalent to an undergraduate degree (graduacao) and not have a doctorate degree
Not be taking, in Brazil, another course of the same level intended in PEC-PG, and be able to start the course within the deadline of the Postgraduate Program

Have a clean record, with no debts with CAPES or the Brazilian government; have an updated CV on the Lattes platform; have spent at least 2 years in your country after obtaining a Brazilian diploma or a master's degree funded by a Brazilian funding agency, where applicable

If applying for a master's: must not have been awarded a master's scholarship (sandwich or full) by a Brazilian federal public entity; if applying for a doctorate (sandwich or full): must not have been awarded a doctoral scholarship by a Brazilian federal public entity
Meet the Call Notice requirements and the specific requirements of the Graduate Program (PPG) of your interest, including language requirements
requirements: Meet the Call Notice requirements and the specific requirements of the Graduate Program (PPG) of your interest, including language requirements.
Wait until December 2026, when CNPq will publish the list of HEIs/ICTs that may receive PEC-PG students.
Check the published list to find out which Graduate Programs (PPGs) are included and what their specific requirements are.
Contact the HEIs/ICTs of your interest, or access their websites, to find out how to apply for a PEC-PG scholarship.
Be ready to start activities in Brazil between March 2027 and March 2028 and comply with all other rules of the Call Notice.
documents: Digital copy of the personal information page from your passport
Proof of CPF (Brazilian Individual Taxpayer Registry) registration status
Proof of residence abroad (such as a water or electricity bill)
Research project in Portuguese, Spanish or English
Complete, updated Lattes CV in Portuguese
A statement of employment, if applicable, updated and issued by the organization or institution where you work, in Portuguese, Spanish or English

A statement from the Graduate Program confirming regular enrollment in a stricto sensu graduate program at the master's or doctoral level, also indicating that your stay in Brazil will not exceed the maximum period stipulated for the defense of your dissertation or thesis
selection_criteria: Selection is two-stage: CNPq first approves the eligible HEIs/ICTs (preliminary list November 2026, final list December 2026), then each HEI/ICT conducts its own selection of candidates.

Applicants are assessed only by the receiving institution's selection process, so the assessment criteria are those of the individual Graduate Program (PPG), applied together with the Call Notice rules; the official page publishes no central scoring rubric.
coverage: Monthly stipend of R$ 2,100.00 (Master's, 24 months) or R$ 3,100.00 (Doctorate, 48 months)
Free place in a Brazilian Higher Education Institution for a postgraduate course
Access to the Brazilian Public Health System (SUS) on the same conditions as Brazilian citizens

Financial aid to return to the country of origin, paid by MRE depending on budgetary and financial availability, with amounts set by country of origin in the table attached to MRE Ordinance No. 572/2024
application_method: STEP 1: Wait until December 2026, when CNPq will publish the list of HEIs/ICTs that may receive PEC-PG students.
STEP 2: Check the list of HEIs/ICTs to find out which Graduate Programs (PPGs) are included and what their specific requirements are.
STEP 3: Contact the HEIs/ICTs of your interest, or access their websites, to find out how to apply for a PEC-PG scholarship.
STEP 4: Await the results of the selection process conducted by the HEI/ICT.
STEP 5: Prepare to come to Brazil and start your activities between March 2027 and March 2028.
official.application_route: Apply directly to the chosen Brazilian institution's own PEC-PG selection process once CNPq publishes the eligible HEI/ICT list in December 2026; the application itself is free.
official.citizenship_residency: Must be a national of, and live in, one of the countries participating in the Program (countries with an educational, cultural, or scientific and technological cooperation agreement in force with Brazil); must not have Brazilian nationality, including dual Brazilian nationality or the right to it, and must not hold a permanent residence permit for Brazil.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme offers scholarships for foreign students; eligibility excludes anyone with Brazilian nationality (including dual nationality or a right to it) or a Brazilian permanent residence permit.
official.research_requirement: A research project in Portuguese, Spanish or English is among the documents required, and the Graduate Program must confirm that the stay in Brazil will not exceed the maximum period stipulated for the dissertation or thesis defense.
official.duration: 24 months for Master's degree; 48 months for Doctorate degree
official.description: The Brazilian Program for Exchange Students - Postgraduate Level (PEC-PG) offers scholarships for foreign students to pursue stricto sensu postgraduate courses at Brazilian Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), and is a modality of the Brazilian Program for Exchange Students (PEC), an official program of the Brazilian government. It is administered in partnership by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MRE), through the Division of Educational Cooperation, the Ministry of Education (MEC), through CAPES, and the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MCTI), through CNPq.
official.region: Host country Brazil; multi-country origin - any of the participating countries with an educational, cultural, or scientific and technological cooperation agreement in force with Brazil (76 countries listed: Africa 29, Latin America and Caribbean 27, Asia 13, Europe 7)
official.program_type: Government scholarship - Brazilian Program for Exchange Students - Postgraduate Level (PEC-PG), run by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Itamaraty) with CNPq and CAPES

not_confirmed: deadline_central - the official pages publish no single applicant deadline; selection deadlines are set by each eligible HEI/ICT from December 2026
study_mode - full-time/part-time status is not stated on the official pages
individual institution/PPG selection deadlines and criteria - published only by each selected HEI/ICT from December 2026

exact travel-aid amounts in the table attached to MRE Ordinance No. 572/2024 - the in.gov.br page was unreachable after 2 attempts; only the aid's existence, conditionality and per-country basis are published on the MRE page
verification.notes: Stipend values (R$ 2,100 master's / R$ 3,100 doctorate per month), calendar, eligibility, benefits and document list taken from the official MRE PEC-PG selection-process page (updated 7 July 2026) and cross-checked with the CNPq Call Notice 16/2026 page and the MRE About-the-program page.

applicant_utility.summary: PEC-PG pays a fixed monthly stipend - R$ 2,100 for a master's and R$ 3,100 for a doctorate plus a free postgraduate place and SUS public-health access; it is not a fully funded award, so flights, visa costs, housing deposits and any spending above the stipend stay on your budget. For the 2027 round there is no central application: CNPq publishes the eligible institutions in December 2026 and each institution then runs its own candidate selection, meaning your real deadlines are set by the Graduate Program you target. Build your Lattes CV, ORCID, CPF status and research project before December 2026, then apply to several eligible programmes at once because institutional capacity is limited.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Graduates living in one of the 76 participating countries who want a Brazilian master's or doctorate and can live on a modest stipend while covering their own travel and setup costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Create or fully update your Lattes CV in Portuguese and gather an updated CV version for institutional selections
Obtain a valid ORCID iD and confirm it resolves to your record
Sort out CPF (Brazilian Individual Taxpayer Registry) registration and keep proof of its status ready
Draft your research project in Portuguese, Spanish or English and align it with the research lines of at least two target PPGs
Prepare a scan of your passport information page and a recent proof of residence abroad (utility bill)
From December 2026, shortlist eligible PPGs from the CNPq list, collect each institution's own deadline and document set, and email the PPG offices early
common_rejection_risks: Any Brazilian nationality, dual nationality or right to it, or a Brazilian permanent residence permit - automatic exclusion
Debts with CAPES or the Brazilian government, or an unclear record
A previous full or sandwich master's or doctoral scholarship from a Brazilian federal public entity at the level being applied for
Failing the individual PPG's own entry requirements, especially its language requirement and research-line fit
Applying to a programme that is not on CNPq's December 2026 eligible list, or missing that institution's own selection window between December 2026 and March 2028
Incomplete document set (missing CPF proof, ORCID, Lattes CV, research project or the PPG enrollment statement), which blocks the scholarship from being paid even after approval
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: International airfare to and from Brazil, visa and migration fees, first-months housing and deposits, local transport and daily living above the R$ 2,100-3,100 monthly stipend, plus any academic material or health costs outside SUS coverage; the return-travel aid is paid by MRE only as budget allows, so treat it as a bonus rather than funded.
document_audit: Research project is accepted only in Portuguese, Spanish or English - translate it beforehand if your project exists in another language
Proof of residence abroad is exemplified by a utility bill (water or electricity); bank statements or employer letters are not listed as substitutes
The Lattes CV must be complete, updated and in Portuguese, which usually means translating publications and project descriptions
The employment statement must be issued by your employer and confirm your stay in Brazil will not exceed the period allowed for the dissertation or thesis defence
A statement from the Graduate Program confirming regular enrollment is required before the scholarship starts being paid, so approval alone does not start the money
alerts: The official calendar carries an explicit warning that dates may change - confirm against the Call Notice (Chamada No. 16/2026) and the CNPq institutional list
Nothing is open to individual applicants until December 2026; institution applications to CNPq closed on 13 August 2026, so ignore early-cycle deadlines quoted by aggregators
Watch for the two-year home-country residence rule if you previously held a Brazilian-funded undergraduate or master's qualification
The return-travel aid depends on MRE budget availability and varies by country of origin - do not count on a fixed sum
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: No central form: from December 2026 pick an eligible PPG from CNPq's published list, apply through that institution's own selection process, then after selection and enrollment submit the required document set to start receiving the monthly stipend, with implementation permitted between March 2027 and March 2028.
